=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md:185-188, 535-538 | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The dead-base trigger treats a deleted base branch as unmerged even when its PR was merged, causing an unnecessary rebuild.
  WHY: Condition (b) fires regardless of merge state, contradicting D13's “closes without merging” scope; severity disagreement: Gemini rated this BLOCKER while the others rated it MAJOR, so the highest severity is used.
- docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md:535-538, 544 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: When the base branch is deleted, rebuild step 2 runs `git diff origin/<base>...origin/<project branch>` against a ref that no longer exists, and the plan gives no recovery path for that failure.
  WHY: The documented BLOCKED path covers `git apply --3way --check` failure, not the earlier `git diff` failure.
- docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md:548-549 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The plan treats closing the old final PR as authorized because “the chain” opened it, although the fresh stage session performing the close did not open it.
  WHY: Under the cited §23.C and §28.C rules, closing a PR not opened by the current session is ask-first, which can leave an unattended stage stalled at a permission prompt.
- docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md:536-538 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The plan does not specify fetch/prune behavior before the branch-presence check, so stale or missing remote state may cause an incorrect dead-base result.
  WHY: The review identifies both a stale remote-tracking ref making the base appear present and a missing fetch making it appear gone.
- docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md:533-538 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The dead-base check performs a REST read at each stage start and project check-in without reusing a cache for repeated checks.
  WHY: For a long-lived project on a non-default base, the per-iteration reads accumulate and add rate-limit pressure.
- docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md:542 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The plan does not specify how rebuild branch suffixes are enumerated or bound when resolving name collisions.
  WHY: Repeated rebuilds or an unavailable default branch leave suffix selection and its failure path unspecified.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "The chain rebuilds the project on the default branch by itself when the project's diff applies cleanly, and records an auto-decision (§28.D)."
  expected_change_site: docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: Proposed D13 logic has correctness flaws in dead-base detection and runtime permission risks when closing the old final PR.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md: Lines 185-188 (D13 decision) vs. lines 536-538 (dead-base trigger) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The dead-base trigger's branch-gone condition can rebuild a project whose named-base PR was merged and whose head branch was auto-deleted.
  WHY: This contradicts D13's scope of closing without merging and can cause an unnecessary rebuild.
- docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md: Lines 536-538 (trigger condition b) vs. line 544 (rebuild step 2) | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: Rebuild step 2 runs `git diff origin/<base>...origin/<project branch>` when the base branch is gone, but no BLOCKED path is documented for this `git diff` failure.
  WHY: A fresh stage session cannot resolve `origin/<base>`, so the rebuild stalls before the documented `--check` failure path.
- docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md: Lines 548-549 | severity=high | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The plan says closing the old final PR is not ask-first because “the chain” opened it, although the fresh stage session did not open it.
  WHY: The permission system may prompt for closing a PR the current session did not open, stalling an unattended stage.
- docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md: Lines 536-538 and 544 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The deleted-base rebuild path has no documented `git diff` recovery, and the plan does not specify whether to fetch/prune before checking the remote branch.
  WHY: A stale remote-tracking ref could falsely keep the base looking alive, while a missing fetch could make it appear gone.
- docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md: Lines 533-538 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The dead-base check performs one REST read at every issue-mode stage start and project check-in without citing a batching or caching pattern.
  WHY: Repeated checks on a long-lived project add API pressure.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md: 535-538, 544 | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: Dead-base detection can trigger for a merged base branch that was deleted, and the rebuild command fails when that deleted branch is used as a diff ref.
  WHY: The OR condition treats a merged-and-deleted branch as dead; the subsequent `git diff origin/<base>...origin/<project branch>` has no documented recovery path.
- docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md: 548-549 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The plan treats closing the old final PR as authorized because the chain opened it, though the rebuild runs in a fresh stage session.
  WHY: The session did not open the PR, so the close can prompt for permission and stall unattended execution.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "The chain rebuilds the project on the default branch by itself when the project's diff applies cleanly, and records an auto-decision (§28.D)."
  Expected change site: docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md
  Evidence of absence: The proposed implementation for D13 logic contains critical correctness flaws and runtime permission risks that prevent it from functioning as described.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md: lines 535-538 (dead-base trigger) and line 544 (rebuild step 2) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: When trigger (b) detects a deleted base branch, rebuild step 2 uses `origin/<base>`, which no longer resolves, and no BLOCKED path is documented for the `git diff` failure.
  WHY: The fresh stage session cannot resolve the deleted base ref, so `git diff` exits non-zero before `git apply --3way --check` runs.
- docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md: lines 535-538 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The branch-gone condition can trigger a rebuild when the named-base PR was merged and GitHub auto-deleted its head branch.
  WHY: The OR condition broadens D13 from “closes without merging” to “closes OR is gone,” causing a redundant rebuild.
- docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md: line 548-549 ("The chain opened it, so this is not a §23.C ask") | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The plan says closing the old final PR is not ask-first because the chain opened it, although the stage session performing the close did not open it.
  WHY: The unattended session can encounter a permission prompt when closing a PR opened by an earlier stage session.
- docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md: line 542 (rebuild step 1: "Create `<project branch>-main` from `origin/<default>` (append `-2`, `-3`, … when taken)") | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The plan does not specify how to enumerate existing branch suffixes, bound suffix selection, or handle an unavailable default branch.
  WHY: A rebuild with repeated collisions or an unfetchable default branch has no documented failure path.
- docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md: lines 533-538 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The dead-base check performs a REST read at every issue-mode stage start and check-in without reusing a cycle-local cache.
  WHY: On a long-lived non-default base, per-iteration reads add rate-limit pressure.
